title: Association of HPV16 infection with p53 and survivin expression in oral squamous cell carcinoma

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between p53 and survivin expression, clinicopathologic parameters and HPV16 infection in OSCC in order to elucidate the potential role of HPV16 in its pathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study enrolled 45 patients who underwent surgical treatment for histologically confirmed OSCC. All patients were followed for three years after primary treatment.
analysis.methods: DNA extracted from FFPE tumor tissues was analyzed for HPV16 genome presence using polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Tumor specimens were formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded (FFPE) and histologically analyzed using hematoxylin/eosin staining. Immunohistochemistry for p53 and survivin was performed using the DAKO system.
analysis.main_results: No statistically significant associations were observed between p53 or survivin expression and clinicopathologic parameters including age, gender, tumor site, grade, stage, recurrence, metastasis or HPV16 status (P > 0.05). A significant correlation was detected between p53 and survivin expression (P = 0.04). HPV16 positivity was significantly associated with the absence of p53 immunoreactivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that HPV16-independent oncogenic pathways are likely predominant in OSCC, while HPV16 infection may be associated with a distinct molecular subset characterized by absent p53 expression (p53−; survivin+/−; HPV16+).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results underscore the biological heterogeneity of OSCC and may have implications for future biomarker-based stratification of patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report on the limitations of the study design.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between HPV16 infection and the expression of p53 and survivin in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The research aimed to understand the potential role of HPV16 in OSCC pathogenesis. The study included 45 patients with histologically confirmed OSCC, and tumor specimens were analyzed using immunohistochemistry and PCR. Results showed no significant associations between p53 or survivin expression and clinicopathologic parameters, but a significant correlation between p53 and survivin expression was observed. HPV16 positivity was linked to the absence of p53 immunoreactivity. The findings suggest that HPV16 may be associated with a specific molecular subset of OSCC, while other oncogenic pathways are more prevalent. These results highlight the heterogeneity of OSCC and may inform future biomarker-based patient stratification. The evidence is based on an abstract-only review, and the study's limitations are not explicitly detailed.

title: Distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus and its association with cervical cytological abnormalities in women from Northeast India

analysis.research_question_and_background: Despite the high incidence of cervical cancer in India, there aren't enough studies on the prevalence of the human papillomavirus (HPV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study aimed at assessing the prevalence of high-risk HPV (hrHPV) types and their association with cytological abnormalities among the adult women of Barak Valley, Northeast India.
analysis.methods: Material and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 562 women aged 18–50+ years and screened for nine high-risk HPV genotypes and liquid-based cytology (LBC) classified by the cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) system.
analysis.main_results: Abnormal cytology was found in 10.1% of women in the order of CIN 1 (5.9%), CIN 2 (3.0%), and CIN 3 (1.2%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Bivariate analysis identified women reporting: nulliparous (Odds ratio [OR] = 2.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.27-3.85), high-parity (OR = 3.7, 95% CI = 2.11-6.5), irregular menstruation (OR = 4.72, 95% CI= 2.94-7.56), history of warts (OR = 13.8, 95% CI = 8.17-23.2), and pregnancy failure (OR = 2.33, 95% CI = 1.34-4.06) had a higher risk of acquiring HPV positivity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study found a high burden of hrHPV and emphasises adopting comprehensive approaches for effective cervical cancer prevention by increasing awareness, providing vaccinations, routine screenings, implementing national policies, and funding better healthcare facilities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This deterministic extraction is based on abstract only. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

analysis.summary_en: Despite the high incidence of cervical cancer in India, there aren't enough studies on the prevalence of the human papillomavirus (HPV). The study aimed at assessing the prevalence of high-risk HPV (hrHPV) types and their association with cytological abnormalities among the adult women of Barak Valley, Northeast India. Material and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 562 women aged 18–50+ years and screened for nine high-risk HPV genotypes and liquid-based cytology (LBC) classified by the cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) system. Abnormal cytology was found in 10.1% of women in the order of CIN 1 (5.9%), CIN 2 (3.0%), and CIN 3 (1.2%). Bivariate analysis identified women reporting: nulliparous (Odds ratio [OR] = 2.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.27-3.85), high-parity (OR = 3.7, 95% CI = 2.11-6.5), irregular menstruation (OR = 4.72, 95% CI= 2.94-7.56), history of warts (OR = 13.8, 95% CI = 8.17-23.2), and pregnancy failure (OR = 2.33, 95% CI = 1.34-4.06) had a higher risk of acquiring HPV positivity. The study found a high burden of hrHPV and emphasises adopting comprehensive approaches for effective cervical cancer prevention by increasing awareness, providing vaccinations, routine screenings, implementing national policies, and funding better healthcare facilities. This deterministic extraction is based on abstract only. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

title: Role of selected interleukins and hormonal biomarkers in screening for human papillomavirus infection and cervical cancer in women

analysis.research_question_and_background: The roles of immunological and hormonal indicators in screening women with HPV infection and cervical cancer (CC) were investigated. The study aimed to explore potential biomarkers for early detection of HPV-related conditions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The present study was conducted in Diyala Province during the period from January to March 2026. A total of 90 blood samples were collected from women who visited Al-Batoul Teaching Hospital and women's clinics.
analysis.methods: Serum levels of IL-1β, IL-2R, FSH, and estrogen, as well as HPV, were detected using ELISA and the Biorex technique.
analysis.main_results: HPV-infected women represented 43.33% of the participants, women with HPV and CC represented 10.00%, and HPV-negative women represented 46.67%. The highest levels of IL-1β, IL-2R, FSH, and estrogen were observed in women with HPV and CC, followed by HPV-infected women, and then the control group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Exploratory ROC curve analysis showed high within-sample discriminatory performance for IL-1β, IL-2R, FSH, and estrogen in differentiating HPV-infected women from controls and women with HPV-associated cervical cancer from controls.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that IL-1β, IL-2R, FSH, and estrogen may serve as potential biomarkers for HPV infection and cervical cancer screening, though further validation is needed.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cutoff values, sensitivity, and specificity estimates were derived and evaluated using the same study cohort and should therefore be considered exploratory rather than clinically validated diagnostic measures. The evidence is moderate due to the exploratory nature of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the roles of immunological and hormonal indicators in screening for HPV infection and cervical cancer in women. Conducted in Diyala Province from January to March 2026, it collected 90 blood samples and used ELISA and Biorex techniques to measure serum levels of IL-1β, IL-2R, FSH, and estrogen, alongside HPV status. Results showed that 43.33% of participants were HPV-infected, 10.00% had HPV and cervical cancer, and 46.67% were HPV-negative. The highest levels of IL-1β, IL-2R, FSH, and estrogen were observed in women with HPV and cervical cancer, followed by HPV-infected women, and then the control group. Exploratory ROC curve analysis indicated high discriminatory performance for these biomarkers in differentiating HPV-infected women from controls and those with HPV-associated cervical cancer. However, the cutoff values, sensitivity, and specificity estimates were derived from the same cohort and are considered exploratory. The study highlights the potential of these biomarkers for screening but emphasizes the need for further validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, as previous research had found a high prevalence in the private health system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis.methods: Samples were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had significantly higher rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) than HPV-negative women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previously reported national rates but lower than in the private health system in the same region, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates between healthcare systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform public health surveillance and resource allocation by providing age-stratified prevalence data, which can guide targeted screening and prevention strategies for HPV-related diseases in the public health system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias as only women attending gynecological check-ups were included, and the evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the report.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined the prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in 39,512 women attending Chile's public health system between 2020-2024. The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 13.70%, with significantly higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had markedly increased rates of cytological abnormalities, including LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women. The prevalence was similar to national rates but lower than previously reported in the private health system, suggesting potential healthcare disparities. These findings provide valuable data for public health planning and targeted screening programs.

title: Effectiveness of motivational interviewing in reducing unmet reproductive health needs among women with human papillomavirus infection: A triple-blind randomized controlled trial

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of motivational interviewing (MI) in reducing unmet reproductive health needs among women with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A triple-blind randomized controlled trial was conducted in 2023 with confirmed HPV infection attending a women's clinic in Iran. Sixty-two women were included, and they were randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving five weekly individual MI sessions or a control group receiving routine education.
analysis.methods: Reproductive health needs were assessed at baseline and five weeks after the intervention using a validated questionnaire. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to compare post-intervention outcomes after adjusting for baseline scores.
analysis.main_results: Compared with the control group, women receiving MI showed significantly lower total reproductive health needs scores after the intervention (P <0.001), with a large effect size (partial η 2 =0.642). Significant improvements were observed across all 12 domains, particularly in psychological health education, male involvement in reproductive health, and women's empowerment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that MI effectively reduced unmet reproductive health needs among women with HPV infection, suggesting its potential integration into routine sexual and reproductive healthcare.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the integration of motivational interviewing into routine sexual and reproductive healthcare to enhance counseling, psychological support, and patient empowerment for women with HPV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single clinic in Iran, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is of moderate strength due to the limited sample size and potential for bias in a non-randomized setting.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of motivational interviewing (MI) in reducing unmet reproductive health needs among women with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. A triple-blind randomized controlled trial was conducted in 2023 with 62 participants attending a women's clinic in Iran. Women were randomly assigned to receive either five weekly MI sessions or routine education. Reproductive health needs were measured using a validated questionnaire at baseline and five weeks post-intervention. The results showed that MI significantly reduced total reproductive health needs scores compared to routine education (P <0.001), with a large effect size. Improvements were observed across all 12 domains, particularly in psychological health education, male involvement, and women's empowerment. The authors concluded that MI could be integrated into routine sexual and reproductive healthcare to improve counseling and patient empowerment. The study's limitations include its single-center setting and potential for bias, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is of moderate strength due to these factors.

title: High diagnostic concordance between vulvar and cervical samples for human papillomavirus detection: a cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of cervical HPV testing, particularly in resource-limited settings, by evaluating the diagnostic concordance between vulvar and cervical samples for HPV detection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 719 paired vulvar and cervical specimens from women, with the goal of assessing the utility of vulvar sampling as an alternative to cervical sampling for HPV testing.
analysis.methods: The researchers retrospectively evaluated vulvar and cervical specimens using clinically validated fluorescence PCR to assess concordance between sampling sites.
analysis.main_results: High-risk HPV (hrHPV) positivity was 47.98% in vulvar samples and 43.53% in cervical samples, with strong site-to-site concordance (κ = 0.821). The negative predictive value of vulvar hrHPV testing for concurrent cervical hrHPV positivity was 95.72%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The high concordance between vulvar and cervical HPV testing suggests that vulvar sampling could be a viable alternative for identifying women at low likelihood of concurrent cervical hrHPV positivity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of non-invasive HPV testing strategies, particularly for women who have difficulty accessing or accepting cervical sampling.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on a single center, which may limit generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of prospective validation and population-based endpoints.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated the diagnostic concordance between vulvar and cervical samples for human papillomavirus (HPV) detection. The researchers analyzed 719 paired specimens using fluorescence PCR and found strong agreement (κ = 0.821) between vulvar and cervical HPV testing. High-risk HPV positivity was observed in 47.98% of vulvar samples and 43.53% of cervical samples, with a negative predictive value of 95.72% for vulvar testing. The results suggest that vulvar sampling could serve as a non-invasive alternative to cervical sampling, particularly for women with limited access or low acceptance of cervical testing. However, the study is retrospective and based on a single center, which may limit its generalizability. Further prospective validation is needed before broader implementation.

title: Self-collected cervical samples for detection of high-risk human papillomavirus: A community outreach approach in a remote region

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background and objectives Self collection of cervical samples is evolving as a potential screening approach to overcome cultural, geographical and logistical barriers that contribute to poor screening uptake.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a study to compare performance of self and physician-collected cervical samples for high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV) detection through community outreach approach in the hilly terrains of Sikkim. A prospective longitudinal study was conducted for 2 y, sampling 210 sexually active women aged 18-65 y attending Central Referral Hospital and 3 district hospitals in Sikkim. Women who had total hysterectomy, diagnosed with cancer or were pregnant were excluded.
analysis.methods: Paired self and physician collected cervical samples were taken from consenting women for HPV DNA and pap test.
analysis.main_results: Result Prevalence of HPV (HPV DNA ± pap) was 17% (36/210) in this study of which HPV 16 was the most common variant (n=4,15%). Physician collected samples had the highest HPV detection rate (n=26,12%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Interpretation and conclusions Performance of physician-sampling was better than self-sampling and pap in the detection of hr-HPV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Physician-sampling should be used for HPV DNA detection when feasible.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Women lost to follow up for colposcopy was 36% (n=13).

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of self-collected cervical samples compared to physician-collected samples for detecting high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV) in a remote region of Sikkim. The research focused on improving screening uptake by addressing cultural, geographical, and logistical barriers. A prospective longitudinal study was conducted over two years, involving 210 sexually active women aged 18-65 years. The study found that HPV prevalence was 17%, with HPV 16 being the most common variant. Physician-collected samples showed higher HPV detection rates and better sensitivity and specificity compared to self-sampling and pap tests. title: Knowledge, attitude and practice on human papilloma virus vaccination: A cross-sectional study among second year MBBS students in India

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection remains a major public health concern because of its strong association with cervical cancer and other HPV-related malignancies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Therefore, it is of interest to assess the knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding HPV vaccination among 150 second-year MBBS students using a questionnaire-based cross-sectional design.
analysis.methods: The study employed a questionnaire-based cross-sectional design to assess knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding HPV vaccination among 150 second-year MBBS students.
analysis.main_results: Most participants showed good awareness of cervical cancer and HPV vaccination, with 96.7% having heard of cervical cancer and 93.3% correctly identifying the primary purpose of HPV vaccination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A positive attitude toward vaccination was observed, as 95.3% supported inclusion of the HPV vaccine in the routine immunization schedule, although important gaps remained regarding high-risk groups, vaccination timing and personal vaccine uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of strengthening medical education and training to improve HPV vaccination awareness and cervical cancer prevention practices among future healthcare professionals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and self-reported data, which may introduce bias and limit the ability to establish causal relationships.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding HPV vaccination among 150 second-year MBBS students in India. The study found that most participants had good awareness of cervical cancer and HPV vaccination, with 96.7% having heard of cervical cancer and 93.3% correctly identifying the primary purpose of HPV vaccination. A positive attitude toward vaccination was observed, as 95.3% supported its inclusion in the routine immunization schedule. However, important gaps remained regarding high-risk groups, vaccination timing, and personal vaccine uptake. The study highlights the need for improved medical education and training to enhance HPV vaccination awareness and cervical cancer prevention practices among future healthcare professionals. The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias and limit causal inference. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study's design and the nature of the data collected.

title: System Pharmacology Profiling of Plumbago zeylanica Linn. Against HPV-Associated Cervical Cancer

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a significant contributor to cancer-related deaths in women globally, with persistent infection by high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) identified as its principal etiological driver.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study explored the mechanistic basis of Plumbago zeylanica’s potential anti-cervical cancer activity through a combined network pharmacology and molecular docking framework targeting HPV-associated pathogenic processes.
analysis.methods: Bioactive phytoconstituents of P. zeylanica were systematically compiled from published literature and the IMPPAT 2.0 database, then filtered through ADME criteria to retain compounds meeting drug-likeness thresholds. Putative protein targets for the shortlisted compounds were obtained via SwissTargetPrediction and SEA platforms, while genes linked to HPV-driven cervical carcinogenesis were sourced from the GeneCards repository using curated disease- and pathogen-specific search terms. Overlapping targets were mapped and used to construct a Protein–Protein Interaction (PPI) network, from which hub genes were identified through topological parameter analysis.
analysis.main_results: Topological analysis of the PPI network highlighted JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as critical regulatory nodes within HPV-mediated oncogenic and inflammatory cascades. Pathway enrichment pointed to significant involvement of cancer-related pathways, TNF signalling, programmed cell death, immune checkpoint modulation, and viral infection mechanisms. Among the docked compounds, zeylanone emerged as the most promising candidate, displaying robust binding affinity toward JUN (−10.2 kcal/mol) and EGFR (−9.0 kcal/mol), while plumbagin, formononetin, diosmetin, and hispidulin also demonstrated favourable docking profiles against multiple targets.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Collectively, these results indicate that Plumbago zeylanica may interfere with cervical cancer progression by simultaneously modulating several HPV-associated oncogenic signalling nodes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that Plumbago zeylanica may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for HPV-associated cervical cancer by targeting key oncogenic and inflammatory pathways.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nonetheless, rigorous in vitro and in vivo experimental validation remains essential to substantiate its clinical translational value.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential anti-cervical cancer activity of Plumbago zeylanica through a network pharmacology and molecular docking approach, focusing on HPV-associated pathogenic processes. The research aimed to identify the mechanistic basis of its therapeutic effects by analyzing bioactive compounds and their interactions with key proteins involved in HPV-mediated oncogenesis and inflammation. The methods included compiling phytoconstituents, filtering them using ADME criteria, identifying protein targets via computational platforms, and constructing a PPI network to pinpoint critical regulatory nodes. The main results highlighted JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as key targets, with zeylanone showing the strongest binding affinity. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that P. zeylanica may modulate multiple HPV-associated oncogenic pathways, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for cervical cancer. However, they emphasized the need for further experimental validation to confirm clinical relevance. The study contributes to understanding the molecular mechanisms of natural remedies against HPV-associated cervical cancer, offering insights for future research and drug development.

title: A Gender-Oriented Approach to Human Papillomavirus Vaccination: A Cross-Sectional Study Among Preclinical Medical Students

analysis.scope_and_question: The first line of defense against cervical cancer is human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. This study aimed to examine preclinical medical students’ gender-based perspectives on the current HPV vaccination program and to assess the potential impact of gender-based approaches to cervical cancer prevention programs on their knowledge of HPV vaccination recommendations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Materials and Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study assessed preclinical medical students’ awareness of HPV vaccination recommendations. The HPV Knowledge Scale was administered to eligible preclinical students. Incomplete questionnaires were excluded from the analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: A total of 448 questionnaires were analyzed, corresponding to an 88.3% response rate. Regarding the recommendation of the HPV vaccine for males aged 11–26 years, only 34.8% of male students (n=46) and 31.0% of female students (n=98) correctly identified this indication. For females aged 11–26 years, the proportion of correct responses was higher, at 60.6% (n=80) among male students and 69.3% (n=219) among female students. Improving medical students’ knowledge of vaccination programs is an important step toward achieving primary prevention, a key objective of public health practice.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Our findings demonstrate that preclinical medical students have lower awareness of HPV vaccination recommendations for males than for females, indicating an urgent need to strengthen gender-neutral HPV vaccination content in undergraduate medical education.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The perception that HPV vaccination is primarily intended for women hinders progress in the fight against HPV.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated preclinical medical students’ gender-based perspectives on HPV vaccination programs and their knowledge of recommendations. The study found that awareness of HPV vaccination for males was significantly lower than for females, with only 34.8% of male students and 31.0% of female students correctly identifying the recommendation for males aged 11–26 years. For females, correct responses were higher, at 60.6% and 69.3% among male and female students, respectively. The study highlights the need to improve gender-neutral education on HPV vaccination to enhance public health prevention efforts. The findings suggest that current educational materials may not adequately address male-targeted vaccination recommendations, potentially limiting the effectiveness of cervical cancer prevention programs.

title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV)-Infected Epithelial Cells and FBLN1-Positive Fibroreticular Cells Govern the Immunogenic Tumor Microenvironment in HPV-Associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma

analysis.research_question_and_background: HPV-associated OPSCC is typically associated with a more favorable prognosis and improved response to therapy than non-HPV–associated OPSCC; however, the underlying differences in the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain incompletely understood.Methods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study advances understanding of TME dynamics in OPSCC and may inform future therapeutic strategies.
analysis.methods: To investigate cellular and molecular factors associated with improved outcomes in HPV-associated OPSCC, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics on samples from two non-HPV–associated OPSCCs, five HPV-associated OPSCCs, and three normal tonsils, with a particular focus on fibroreticular cells (FRCs).Results.
analysis.main_results: Spatial mapping demonstrated that FBLN1-positive FRCs were closely associated with both tumor and immune cells, suggesting a role in promoting an immunogenic TME.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In addition, HPV-associated OPSCC exhibited higher levels of proliferating epithelial cells and increased expression of antigen-presentation genes than non-HPV–associated tumors.Conclusion.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Enhanced antigen presentation and epithelial proliferation may facilitate tumor-immune interactions, potentially contributing to improved clinical outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings highlight the potential role of FBLN1-positive FRCs in promoting immune activation within the TME of HPV-associated OPSCC.

analysis.summary_en: HPV-associated OPSCC is typically associated with a more favorable prognosis and improved response to therapy than non-HPV–associated OPSCC; however, the underlying differences in the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain incompletely understood.Methods. This study advances understanding of TME dynamics in OPSCC and may inform future therapeutic strategies. To investigate cellular and molecular factors associated with improved outcomes in HPV-associated OPSCC, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics on samples from two non-HPV–associated OPSCCs, five HPV-associated OPSCCs, and three normal tonsils, with a particular focus on fibroreticular cells (FRCs).Results. Spatial mapping demonstrated that FBLN1-positive FRCs were closely associated with both tumor and immune cells, suggesting a role in promoting an immunogenic TME. In addition, HPV-associated OPSCC exhibited higher levels of proliferating epithelial cells and increased expression of antigen-presentation genes than non-HPV–associated tumors.Conclusion. Enhanced antigen presentation and epithelial proliferation may facilitate tumor-immune interactions, potentially contributing to improved clinical outcomes. These findings highlight the potential role of FBLN1-positive FRCs in promoting immune activation within the TME of HPV-associated OPSCC.
